PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

2.. Presentation - National Breast Cancer Awareness Month in the City of Commerce Moyra Garcia, Social Services Coordinator, gave a brief introduction, followed by a presentation from Maritza Quevedo of FHCCGLA on Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Moyra Garcia also expressed gratitude to the Public Safety Division for supporting the cause through the Pink Patch Project.

Councilmember Rebollo thanked everyone for the presentation and inquired about mammograms, asking if community members could receive them for free. The response was positive, and she suggested partnering on social media platforms to raise awareness and encourage residents to get exams, emphasizing collaboration to keep the community informed.

Mayor Argumedo read a proclamation.  

1.. City Videos Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz gave a brief introduction to the Fiesta Padres event, followed by a video presentation. 

PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoyotl inquired about the removal of greenery from the park, noting that the project manager did not address where the trees would be relocated.

Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk, Shumway, read a comment submitted via email from Lela Leon regarding Item #7, which expressed concerns about parking in the village.

SCHEDULED MATTERS

6.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Duarte provided an overview of activities from the past two weeks and mentioned that an update on the Flock system would be presented at the next meeting.

Councilmember Rebollo raised concerns about reports of encampments at Bristow Park, particularly around the picnic shelters at night. She requested that a team be sent to conduct outreach in the area.

7.. Update and Consideration of Parking Shortage at Village Neighborhood  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Public Safety Manager Edson provided an overview, noting that 51% of the distributed surveys had been returned.

In response to Councilmember Lainez’s question about whether the code amendment could be limited to a specific neighborhood or apply citywide, City Manager Hernandez explained that the City Council could choose to focus on one neighborhood, apply the change to the entire city, or implement it as a pilot project. Regarding permit parking, Councilmember Lainez pointed out that the survey results were not favorable, citing challenges such as staffing, managing, and rolling out the program. He also raised concerns that permit parking might overburden other neighborhoods and suggested that widening driveways might be the best solution. Additionally, he recommended exploring "T-making," which could prevent oversized vehicles from parking on the street and help eliminate double-parking by residents.

Mayor Argumedo agreed that option three was the most viable solution. He emphasized the importance of developing appropriate standards and moving forward with the plan, which would include allowing driveways to be used as additional parking spaces. He also supported the idea of T-making to address parking issues.

Councilmember Garcia sought clarification, asking if selecting option three would mean no further parking regulation changes would occur in that neighborhood.

Councilmember Rebollo suggested that widening driveways should be considered for other neighborhoods as well, to help alleviate street parking congestion.

Councilmember Lainez recommended that staff assess where T-making could be implemented across the city, specifically mentioning areas like Bristow Park and Triggs Street for a potential pilot program.

Vice Mayor Altamirano supported option three and the idea of allowing parking in front of driveways to create additional parking spaces. 
City Manager Hernandez added that enforcement could be complaint-based, allowing vehicles to park in front of driveways as long as it wasn’t blocking a resident's own driveway.

City Manager Hernandez concluded by summarizing the Council's preferences: they favored option three, supported exploring T-making and code changes, and suggested evaluating areas like Bristow Park for implementation, along with determining how to enforce parking in front of driveways.





8.. A Sublease Agreement Between the City of Commerce and the Amitim Group, LLC  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Assistant City Manager Domic provided an overview of the staff report.

Vice Mayor Altamirano inquired if the $79,000 could be allocated to a special fund rather than the General Fund. Domic responded that the City Council has the authority to appropriate funds for specific programs and earmark them accordingly.

ORDINANCES

10.. Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance to Approve Development Agreement Related to Commercial Cannabis Permit Application No. 18-047  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Giselle Delgado, Management Analyst, provided an overview of the item. The Mayor then opened and closed the public hearing.

Councilmember Lainez asked for clarification on what determines the annual operating fee. Giselle Delgado explained that this specific business for testing does not bring same revenue as other cannabis businesses and the City Council could potentially reduce fees for this specific business.



11.. Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance to Approve Development Agreement Related to Commercial Cannabis Permit Application No. 18-026 for Commercial Cannabis Testing  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Giselle Delgado, Management Analyst, provided an overview of the staff report. 

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia mentioned that she was unable to attend the Camp Commerce Women’s Getaway but congratulated the participants and staff on organizing a successful event, based on the photos she saw. She also expressed strong support for breast cancer survivors, praising their strength and resilience.

Councilmember Rebollo noted that she was also unable to attend the Women’s Getaway and thanked the City Attorney for donating treats to the retreat. She then requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory of Maria De Los Angeles Garcia.

Councilmember Lainez reported on the recent Neighborhood Watch meeting on Astor Street, highlighting concerns about poor lighting, with streetlights only on one side of the street. Councilmember Lainez also attended the Citadel Commerce Clean-Up event and thanked Commerce Crush, the Unplugged program, and other groups for their participation.

Mayor Argumedo shared that he attended both the Neighborhood Watch meeting and the Citadel Clean-Up event.
